_comment: Single source of truth for latency budgets (TECH-SPEC.md sec 8.4). qa/latency.py and qa/live_ws_turn.py both load this file — never hardcode a copy elsewhere.

measured.providers: STT=faster-whisper tiny.en (local, tuned) / LLM=LiteLLM proxy gpt-oss-120b-groq / TTS=kokoro-local (in-process Kokoro-82M via mlx-audio), CHUNKED synthesis on (PET_TALK_TTS_CHUNKS=1, first chunk 4 words, later chunks 6)
measured.machine: M-series MacBook Pro, server under ~/miniconda3/envs/local-ml-py311. Quiet re-measure attempted per the 12c caveat: `uptime` read 3.93 (1-min) before this pass started. By the time the kept turn-level runs executed, two other opencode lanes had spun up at 200%+ CPU each; a 10-minute bounded wait never got load back under 4 (best point 4.28), and the three kept qa/latency.py runs ran at 1-min load 6.19, 7.48, 6.26 — NOT fully quiet, but a real ~25x drop from 12c's peak of 186. stall_ms improved (695.6ms to 642.2ms p50) but did not clear budget, so the dominant component (STT) is sensitive to ordinary background contention, not only to extreme load — see stall_ms.note.
measured.method: Turn-level only this pass: live WS through the real FastAPI loop, `APP_PORT=8089 python3 qa/latency.py` x3 at N=5 turns, median of the three runs (by stall_ms) kept, real speech from qa/fixtures/weather_turn.wav (1.44s, 16kHz mono). No isolated component-level provider-call script was run this pass; stt/tts per-turn figures come from the server's own telemetry ledger (server/turns.jsonl) for the kept run instead.
measured.stt_ms: NOT MEASURED in isolation this pass — see stall_ms.note for the in-server per-turn STT stage times from server/turns.jsonl (495-870ms across the 15 turns in the three kept-set runs, against 164.1ms p50 in isolation in 12c and 143.4ms on the fully quiet 12b machine)
measured.llm_first_content_ms: NOT MEASURED this pass — unchanged from the 12b row (512.4 p50 / 805.4 p95)
measured.tts_ms: NOT MEASURED in isolation this pass — unchanged from the 12c row (127.3 p50 / 246.1 p95, PASS at p50)

stall_ms.note: Improved from 12c's 695.6ms (load 186) but still FAILs at load ~7. Kept run's own stage receipt (server/turns.jsonl, t-latency-2): stt 590.0ms, stall 639.3ms — stall lands 49.3ms after STT finishes (warm cache working). Dominant component is STT: 164.1ms p50 in isolation in 12c, 143.4ms on the fully quiet 12b machine, but 495-870ms inside the server here while Kokoro's own synthesis threads and two other opencode lanes shared the CPU. STT inside this server is not resilient to ordinary background contention — not only a load-186 artifact as 12c guessed.

first_audio_ms.what: first frame carrying playable audio, agent.chunk or agent.sentence, whichever lands first

turn_worst_ms.note: PASS on all three post-wait runs. warm_stall_cache still doing its job; the stall never pays a cold synth.

notes.live_ws_turn_gate: 1 run this pass: barge ack 1.9ms PASS (budget <=100), time-to-stall 218.9ms PASS (budget <=400). This harness drives the worker in-process against a stub LLM, so it does not see the live-server STT contention in stall_ms above — it proves the queue/cancellation path, not turn-level latency under load.
notes.real_engine_e2e: PET_TALK_REAL_ENGINE=1 qa/test_real_engine_e2e.py 3/3 PASS. kokoro-local synthesised 278,444 bytes of valid RIFF; STT read it back as 'Good morning. Donna Paulson here. Executive Secretary Mode is fully operational.'; a live /ws turn drove Donna through the proxy to 228,044 bytes of playable audio.
notes.not_softened: No budget moved. stall_ms still reads FAIL against its written value — the change this pass is the dominant-component diagnosis, not the number.

history.providers: STT=faster-whisper tiny.en (local, tuned) / LLM=LiteLLM proxy gpt-oss-120b-groq / TTS=kokoro-local (in-process Kokoro-82M via mlx-audio), CHUNKED synthesis on (PET_TALK_TTS_CHUNKS=1, first chunk 4 words, later chunks 6)
history.machine: M-series MacBook Pro, server under ~/miniconda3/envs/local-ml-py311. NOT A QUIET MACHINE: three other P0 lanes were building and testing on the same box throughout. Load average was 186 at the worst point and 16-20 during the runs recorded here, against a load of roughly 2 for the 2026-09-12b row. Every turn-level number below is therefore a CEILING, not this stack's capability, and the stt/stall regressions against 12b are machine load, not code — see the stage receipt in `notes`. Followed up 2026-09-12d: only partially confirmed, see the current measured block above.
history.method: Turn-level: live WS through the real FastAPI loop, `APP_PORT=8089 python3 qa/latency.py` x3 at N=5 turns, median of the three runs, real speech from qa/fixtures/weather_turn.wav (1.44s, 16kHz mono). Component-level: direct provider calls, N=9 for TTS and N=5 for STT, p50/p95. The TTS sentence is 13 words (the brief called it 12; it is 13 by plain split). `tts_ms` now measures the FIRST PLAYABLE AUDIO of a sentence — chunk 0 under chunked synthesis — because that is what a listener waits on; the whole-sentence figure is kept beside it.

stt_ms.note: 143.4 p50 on the quiet machine in the 12b row. Nothing in this lane touched STT.

history.llm_first_content_ms: NOT MEASURED this pass — no component LLM run; unchanged from the 12b row (512.4 p50 / 805.4 p95)

tts_ms.result: PASS at p50; p95 clips the budget
tts_ms.what: time to the first playable audio chunk of a 13-word sentence, kokoro-local, N=9
tts_ms.note: Down from 236.6 p50 by chunked synthesis. The floor is ~110ms of fixed per-call overhead: a 3-word first chunk measured 136.7 p50 and a 2-word one 204.1, both WORSE, so 4 words is the setting. Gated real-engine test measured 174.4 p50 at N=5 on a busier moment.

tts_whole_sentence_ms.note: the same sentence with PET_TALK_TTS_CHUNKS=0. This is what every non-chunking tyre still pays.

stall_ms.note: Machine load, upstream of this lane. One turn's own stage receipt (server/turns.jsonl, t-latency-4): stt 700.3ms, stall 748.2ms — the stall lands 47.9ms after STT finishes, which is the warm cache hit working. On the 12b quiet machine the same path was 245.5ms.

first_audio_ms.what: first frame carrying playable audio, agent.chunk or agent.sentence, whichever lands first

turn_worst_ms.note: The cold-start breach is closed. `warm_stall_cache` pre-synthesizes the persona's stalls at startup (donna, 3 of 3, ~13s after boot, dominated by Kokoro's one-time model load), so the first turn of a fresh process no longer pays a full synth. PASS on all three runs, under load.

notes.live_ws_turn_gate: 3 single-shot runs: 387.8 PASS, 304.0 PASS, 703.7 FAIL against 400ms. Still N=1 and still flaky by design; the third run is the same machine load as stall_ms above.
notes.real_engine_e2e: PET_TALK_REAL_ENGINE=1 qa/test_real_engine_e2e.py 3/3 PASS. kokoro-local synthesised 278,444 bytes of valid RIFF; STT read it back; a live /ws turn drove Donna through the proxy to 210,044 bytes of playable audio.
notes.backward_compat: GET /audio/t-live-qa-1-s1 -> 200 audio/wav, 272,444 bytes on a chunked turn. The re-muxed whole-sentence WAV that audio_url serves is intact, so a client that ignores agent.chunk is unaffected.
notes.not_softened: No budget moved. tts_ms p95, stt_ms and stall_ms all still read FAIL against their written values.

history.providers: STT=faster-whisper tiny.en (local, tuned) / LLM=LiteLLM proxy gpt-oss-120b-groq / TTS=kokoro-local (in-process Kokoro-82M via mlx-audio)
history.method: Turn-level: live WS through the real FastAPI loop, `APP_PORT=8089 python3 qa/latency.py` x3 (N=5 turns each), median of the three runs, real speech from qa/fixtures/weather_turn.wav (1.44s, 16kHz mono). Component-level: direct provider calls (FasterWhisperSTT.transcribe / OpenAICompatibleLLM.stream / KokoroLocalTTS.synth), N=5, p50/p95. TTS sentence is 12 words; STT clip is the same fixture.

llm_first_content_ms.result: PASS at p50; p95 clips the budget — see docs/SPEC.md 9.1

turn_worst_ms.result: PASS warm / FAIL on the first turn of a fresh process

history.method: direct provider calls (GroqSTT.transcribe / OpenAICompatibleLLM.stream / KokoroSpacePilotTTS.synth), N=5, median of 5 (component-level only — see docs/SPEC.md 9.1 for why the live WS turn could not be measured this pass)
history._note: SUPERSEDED by the 2026-09-12b row. Kept as history: this is what the stack measured before the reasoning-token fix (llm), the in-process Kokoro tyre (tts), the tuned local Whisper (stt) and the real-audio fixture (which is why every turn-level metric here reads NOT MEASURED).

stt_streaming.what: Streaming STT (server/stt_stream.py) vs the whole-utterance pass, on the stage 9.1 named as the whole stall_ms breach (stt 590.0ms of 642.2ms). APPENDED, not a replacement: the 2026-09-12d turn-level row above is untouched and still stands.
stt_streaming.harness: qa/test_stt_streaming.py::TestRealEngineStreamingLatency, PET_TALK_REAL_ENGINE=1. COMPONENT-LEVEL, not turn-level: real faster-whisper tiny.en through the real _on_user_chunk/_stream_stop handlers, 20ms chunks paced in real time (what cli/client.py sends), stub TTS + stub LLM. Its 'streaming OFF' column is therefore NOT comparable to the 642.2ms turn-level stall_ms above - it is an A/B of one stage on one clock in one process.
stt_streaming.clip: qa/fixtures/weather_turn.wav repeated to 2.88s @16kHz mono (the 1.44s fixture alone is shorter than two 700ms windows)
stt_streaming.n: 5 turns per mode plus a discarded warm-up, 5 runs kept
stt_streaming.machine: M-series MacBook Pro, ~/miniconda3/envs/local-ml-py311. NOT QUIET: 1-min load 42.3 / 52.4 / 53.4 / 74.3 / 88.2 across the five runs, against ~7 for the 12d row - six other lanes were building in this worktree. Absolute numbers are ceilings; the ON/OFF comparison is the point.

streaming_on_early_stall.note: agent.stall is emitted from the latest partial BEFORE finalization, so stall_ms stops being an STT number: a warm stall-cache lookup and a frame send. PASSED in every run, including load 88.2. Taken with the stall_sent hook pinned by the test harness; that hook has since LANDED in server/turn.py (2026-09-12f), so stt_stream.turn_accepts_stall_sent() now reads True and this path runs whenever PET_TALK_STT_STREAM=1. The numbers above are unchanged by it. Streaming still ships off by default - see docs/SPEC.md 10.

streaming_on_tail_only.note: WORSE than streaming off at this load, and the reason PET_TALK_STT_STREAM defaults to 0. With turn.py still owning the stall it waits for the transcript, and the transcript waits up to PET_TALK_STT_STREAM_WAIT_MS (1200) for an in-flight prefix decode - at load 50+ a prefix decode outlasts the 700ms window, so one is nearly always in flight at user.stop. Dropping that wait instead runs two faster-whisper decodes at once and produced a 2534ms outlier when measured that way.

streaming_off.note: Today's shape on this harness. Not the same number as the 642.2ms turn-level row - no Kokoro, no proxy.

final_transcript_ms.note: Streaming does NOT make the answer start sooner, and has a fatter tail (up to 2136ms) from the in-flight wait. It moves the STALL off the transcript's critical path; claiming more than that would be a fake green.

stt_streaming.turn_level_stall_ms: NOT MEASURED for the streaming path - needs a live server with Kokoro + the LiteLLM proxy at load ~7 AND the server/turn.py stall_sent hook. The 12d turn-level 642.2ms FAIL above is still the standing turn-level number.
stt_streaming.whisperkit: NOT MEASURED. whisperkit-cli is not on PATH and no CoreML model is on disk; the CLI plus model is far over the 200MB this lane was allowed to download. The belief that the Neural Engine must be the fastest tyre is still a belief. Flagged supports_streaming=false regardless: it spawns a process and reloads its model per call.
stt_streaming.deepgram_streaming: OUT OF SCOPE (2026-09-12). Deepgram has a real streaming socket that belongs behind supports_streaming instead of repeated POSTs; this lane fixed the local default first.

stt_streaming_turn_level.what: Turn-level attempt to re-measure the streaming-STT early-stall path now that the server/turn.py stall_sent hook (named in measured.stt_streaming.stall_ms.streaming_on_early_stall.note) has landed. APPENDED, does not touch measured.stall_ms (12d) or measured.stt_streaming (12e).
stt_streaming_turn_level.machine: Bounded 10-min wait for 1-min load < 6 timed out at 10.27, after the load peaked at 435 (six-plus other sessions on this box). Runs below were taken as load fell through 6-14; see per-run loads.
stt_streaming_turn_level.method: APP_PORT=8089 python3 qa/latency.py x3 per mode (N=5), median of the three kept by stall_ms p50, real server (kokoro-local + faster-whisper + LiteLLM proxy), PET_TALK_STT_STREAM=0 then =1.
stt_streaming_turn_level.finding: stall_ms is statistically indistinguishable between modes (223.1ms vs 194.3ms) because this harness never exercises the streaming code path at all: qa/latency.py and qa/live_ws_turn.py both send the whole utterance in one user.stop message and never send a user.chunk frame, so server/ws.py's _stream_stop never has a stream session to serve and every turn falls through to the identical whole-utterance path regardless of PET_TALK_STT_STREAM. Confirmed: zero 'stream' log lines with PET_TALK_STT_STREAM=1, and every turn in server/turns.jsonl for both passes reads path=worker, never path=stream.

live_ws_turn_time_to_stall_ms.result: PASS both, same-harness caveat above applies

stt_streaming_turn_level.real_engine_e2e: 3/3 pass both modes. Kokoro synthesized 278,444 bytes valid RIFF both times; /transcribe read back the same fixed clip identically both times.

final_transcript_comparison.note: Identical in all 6 captured turns, as expected given the finding above - both modes ran the identical decode. Not evidence either way about the streaming path's own accuracy, which is still open per measured.stt_streaming.final_transcript_ms.

stt_streaming_turn_level.decision: PET_TALK_STT_STREAM stays 0. Not because streaming failed a budget this pass - it was never actually driven - but because flipping the default on a measurement that didn't exercise the code path would be a fake green. What's still needed: a turn-level harness that paces user.chunk frames against the live server, the way qa/test_stt_streaming.py already does component-level.
